newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Six killed in attacks in Tajik capital - official.
newsitem.headline: Six killed in attacks in Tajik capital - official.

text.p: Six people were killed and one was injured by unidentified assailants in the Tajikistan capital Dushanbe on Tuesday night, the Interior Ministry said on Wednesday.

A ministry spokesman told Reuters the killings took place in different residential areas in the western part of the city. "We view all the killings as parts of one outrageous act of terrorism," he said.

The spokesman said the dead included a 46-year-old lieutenant-colonel serving with Russian border troops deployed in Tajikistan. Two security workers at the U.S. emabassy in Dushanbe were also among the victims.
A policeman was killed in an attack on the mental hospital he was guarding. The attackers freed one of the patients, Nazhmetdin Alimov, who belonged to a group fighting the government.
Dozens of Russian servicemen and civilians have been killed and wounded in attacks in the Tajik capital since the end of last year.

No one has claimed responsibility for the attacks but they have been widely blamed on fighters of the Islamist opposition who have battled the former Soviet republic's secular government in a four-year civil war.
About 20,000 Russian soldiers carry out peacekeeping duties in Tajikistan and guard its frontier with Afghanistan.
They see themselves as a bulwark against Islamic fundamentalism on Russia's vulnerable southern flank after the loss of territory which followed the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991.

The latest killings occurred only a day after the end of a two-week hostage crisis that highlighted the instability of impoverished Tajikistan, which borders China and Afghanistan. Russian and Western hostages were held by a rebel group in the standoff with the government.
A ceasefire agreed at the end of last year between the Islamist opposition and the Tajik government seems to be holding.
But numerous armed rogue groups often destabilise the situation in the Central Asian state. Western observers say President Imomali Rakhmonov controls only 15-20 percent of the country.
